findings.summary: The host-resolution fallback applies `.split('.')[0]` unconditionally, not only after a cluster-DNS suffix was stripped.
findings.scenario: A stream with a Deployment named `api` and `value: https://api.stripe.com/v1` proposes `Calls web → api` and never proposes `api.stripe.com` at all.

critique.reason: The code applies `.split('.')[0]` unconditionally, leading to the described scenario.

summary: The host-resolution fallback applies `.split('.')[0]` unconditionally, not only after a cluster-DNS suffix was stripped, so any external FQDN whose first label happens to match an in-file workload or Service name is turned into an internal `Calls` edge instead of an External Dependency. · The host-resolution fallback applies `.split('.')[0]` unconditionally, not only after a cluster-DNS suffix was stripped, so any external FQDN whose first label happens to match an in-file workload or Service name is turned into an internal `Calls` edge instead of an External Dependency.
